name: PostgreSQL SQL dialect
summary: The SQL dialect of PostgreSQL: a highly standard-conforming, extensible SQL with user-defined types, operators, index access methods and procedural languages, rich built-in types (arrays, ranges, JSONB), CTEs, window functions, MVCC transactions with serializable snapshot isolation, and descent from Berkeley POSTGRES/PostQUEL.
standards: ISO/IEC 9075:2023 (core conformance target; see Appendix D of the manual)

level_notes.0: One implementation defines the dialect: postgres/postgres (parser in src/backend/parser with the Bison grammar gram.y, planner in src/backend/optimizer, executor in src/backend/executor). Level 0 also lists independent re-implementations and extractions of the dialect's grammar (libpg_query, CockroachDB's sql.y, ANTLR, sqlglot, sqlfluff, sqlparser-rs).
level_notes.1: The PostgreSQL manual (Part II 'The SQL Language' and Part VI 'Reference') is the normative description of the dialect; ISO/IEC 9075 is paywalled, so the ISO catalogue page, Appendix D (conformance) and free BNF extractions are linked. The Berkeley POSTGRES design papers are the defining papers of the system's data model and rule/extension design.
level_notes.2: The official tutorial (Part I) and the manual's Internals part are filed here, with books and courses on internals.
level_notes.3: Encyclopedia and catalogue pages; Rosetta Code only has a generic SQL category.
